claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child in hospital for 15 weeks but claimant regularly spends on child
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning a formal assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! I need to start by asking you about your child or children. 

**How old is your child (or what are the ages of your children)?**

Please tell me:
1. The name(s) of your child/children
2. Their age(s)

This will help me determine which path of the eligibility rules applies to you. Child Benefit rules differ depending on whether a child is:
- **Under 16** - generally eligible
- **16-19** - eligible if in full-time education or approved training
- **20 or older** - generally not eligible

Once you provide this information, I can guide you through the full eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 8 years old and lives with me at home. I just want to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you're asking about **Alex, who is 8 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, he falls into the category where Child Benefit eligibility is generally available. Let me navigate through the next part of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work?**

(Since Alex is 8 years old, I expect the answer would be that he's not in paid work, but I need to confirm this with you.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's only 8, so he's just at primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear - Alex is at primary school and not in any paid work. Let me move forward with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question: **Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?** 

Specifically, is he not receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit (in their own right)

For an 8-year-old at primary school, the answer would typically be "yes" (they're not receiving these benefits), but I need to confirm this with you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name - he's just a child living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since he's 8 years old at primary school, I'd expect the answer to be "no" - he's not in an apprenticeship. Can you confirm this?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 8! He's just going to primary school like any other child his age.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes complete sense. Let me move forward.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. There are several paths that could qualify you. Let me ask:

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

This is the main path - if you live in the UK as your normal place of residence, you would meet the residency requirement. 

If for some reason you don't normally live in the UK, there are other special circumstances that might still allow you to claim (such as Crown service abroad), but let me start with this main question.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm based in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's straightforward - you meet the UK residency requirement. Let me move forward.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Are you responsible for Alex?**

You've already mentioned that Alex lives with you at home in Manchester. This means you satisfy the "living with the child" requirement, which counts as being responsible for the child.

Can you confirm that Alex lives with you and you're providing for his care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely - Alex lives with me at home and I provide for all his needs.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear - you live with Alex and you're responsible for his care. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or trying to claim for him?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent claiming for him?
- Is anyone else (like a grandparent) claiming for him?

Or are you the only person claiming or intending to claim Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex - I'm the only one.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear. Let me move forward.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Where is Alex living?**

Is he:
- Living normally at home with you in Manchester?
- In hospital?
- In care (e.g., residential care, care home)?
- Fostered?

I expect the answer is that he's living normally at home with you, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex has been in hospital for a while now - he's been there for a few months. But I still visit him regularly and buy things for him like clothes and his favorite snacks and magazines.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for sharing that. That's an important detail. Let me navigate to the next check about hospital duration.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Important question about the hospital stay: **Has Alex been in hospital continuously for more than 12 weeks (roughly 3 months)?**

You mentioned he's been there for a few months. I need to check:
- Exactly how long has he been in hospital in total?
- Has he had any breaks out of hospital during this time, and if so, how long were they?

The reason I ask is that Child Benefit can normally continue for up to 12 weeks in hospital, but there's a special cumulative rule. If he returns within 28 days of leaving hospital, any previous stays count towards the 12-week limit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in hospital for about 15 weeks now, so yes, more than 3 months. He's been there the whole time without coming home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex has been in hospital continuously for approximately 15 weeks, which exceeds the 12-week limit. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! There's an important exception to the 12-week rule. Even though Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, Child Benefit can continue if you're **regularly spending money on him while he's in hospital**.

You mentioned earlier that you visit regularly and buy things for him like clothes, snacks, and magazines. 

**Can you confirm: Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital?** This could include:
- Clothes
- Food/snacks
- Entertainment (magazines, books, etc.)
- Any other items or expenses towards his care

This is an important exception that could allow you to continue claiming Child Benefit despite the extended hospital stay.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, definitely - I regularly spend money on him. I buy him clothes, his favorite snacks and treats, magazines to keep him entertained, and other things he needs while he's there. I visit as often as I can and always bring him something.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's very important - your regular spending on Alex while he's in hospital means you can qualify for an exception to the 12-week rule. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Final question: **Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's hospital accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- Is the NHS (or the hospital itself) paying for his care?
- Or is the local council involved in paying for his accommodation/maintenance?

Generally, if the council is paying, you wouldn't be eligible for Child Benefit. But if the NHS or hospital is providing the care (as is typical), and the council isn't paying, then you would be eligible.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything - it's just the NHS hospital providing his care. The council isn't involved at all.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the final piece of the puzzle. Based on all the information you've provided, I can now determine your eligibility. Let me provide you with the outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT**

Great news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

### Summary of Your Situation:

**About Alex:**
- 8 years old (under 16) ✓
- Not working ✓
- Not receiving benefits in his own right ✓
- Not in an apprenticeship ✓

**About You:**
- Normally resident in the UK (Manchester) ✓
- Living with Alex and responsible for his care ✓
- Only person claiming for him ✓

**The Hospital Exception:**
Even though Alex has been in hospital for 15 weeks (longer than the standard 12-week limit), you qualify for an important exception because **you regularly spend money on him** - buying clothes, snacks, magazines, and other items. This regular financial contribution towards his care allows you to continue claiming Child Benefit.

**Council Payment Check:**
The NHS hospital is providing his care, and the local council is not involved in paying for his accommodation or maintenance, so there are no disqualifications. ✓

---

### Next Steps:

1. **If you haven't already claimed**, contact HMRC to start your Child Benefit claim
2. **Keep records** of your regular spending on Alex while he's in hospital (receipts for clothes, snacks, etc.) - these may be useful if HMRC asks about your claim
3. **Notify HMRC** of any significant changes in Alex's circumstances (e.g., when he's discharged from hospital)

### Useful Links:
- [Apply for Child Benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim)
- [Child Benefit information](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit)

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your Child Benefit eligibility?
